characters.name: The Golden man
characters.description: Tall, imperious, and physically imposing with a piercing gaze. He represents the elitist, brutal ideology of the Gold caste, viewing himself as superior to all other humans.
key_events: Delivering a speech to the students about the necessity of strength and the inherent inequality of mankind
Threatening the students that only the fit for power will survive

characters.name: The narrator
characters.description: A member of the low-born Red caste who harbors intense hatred toward the Golds. He is forged by hardship and driven by a promise of vengeance.
key_events: Observing the speech of the Golden man
Reflecting on his own identity and the strength born from his difficult upbringing
Vowing that none of the Golds will survive

relationships.description: The narrator views the Golden man as the embodiment of the oppressive system that brought war to his people, while the Golden man views Reds as inherently weak and subhuman.
moments: The narrator watches the Golden man with hatred while the Golden man unknowingly lectures about the inferiority of the narrator's kind.

world_facts.name: Color Caste System
world_facts.description: A stratified society where humans are divided into colors, with Gold at the top as the ruling class and Red as a lower caste viewed as weak and subservient.

world_facts.name: The Noble Lie of Demokracy
world_facts.description: An ideology dismissed by the Golds as a cancer, which suggests that men are created equal and the strong should nurture the gentle.

world_facts.name: The Institute / Assembly
world_facts.description: A place of learning for elite Golds where they are indoctrinated in the philosophy of power and dominion, though it is implied to be a place of lethal trial.

summary: In the prologue, an unnamed narrator reveals his transformation from a man who once desired peace to one driven by a singular purpose of vengeance. He observes a group of twelve hundred elite students being addressed by a tall, imperious man of the Gold caste—a person the narrator identifies as the architect of his suffering and the harbinger of war. The Golden man delivers a chilling speech to the assembly, decrying the 'Noble Lie' of equality and asserting that the Golds are the pinnacle of evolution, destined to rule over the 'lesser' colors through blood and iron. He threatens the students, warning that they have been soft and shielded from pain, and that they will soon undergo a trial where only the most ruthless will survive. The narrator, observing from the shadows, internalizes the contempt directed at his own kind. He reveals himself to be a Red, a member of the low-born caste whom the Golds view as subhuman and feeble. Contrary to their elitist assumptions, the narrator describes his life in the 'bowels' of a harsh world, noting that he has been forged by fire, hate, and love. As the chapter concludes, he rejects the Gold man's narrative of superiority, confidently declaring that the Golds are wrong about his people and swearing that when the coming conflict concludes, none of the arrogant, gilded oppressors will survive. This establishes the central conflict of a divided, brutalized society where a low-caste revolutionary prepares to challenge the absolute power of the ruling elite.
